clue.text: Extremely short journeys — walks!

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extremities of the next word, its first and last letters

parts.note: rides are journeys on horseback or by vehicle

explanation.surface: A complaint that the walks on offer are only brief outings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely short' gives ST, the outside letters of 'short'.
explanation.definitionFit: Strides are long steps, so the plural noun matches walks as paces taken.

clue.text: Compromise a manager securing rating

indicators.note: securing means holding within, so the letters sit inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A compromise is struck with a manager over a performance rating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rating' looks like an assessment, but in the navy a rating is a non-officer sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: In the British navy a rating is an ordinary sailor without a commission.

clue.text: Cargo coming after soldiers charge again

indicators.note: coming after puts the cargo word behind the soldiers

parts.note: RE, Royal Engineers, are soldiers
a load is a cargo

explanation.surface: Soldiers storm in after a cargo shipment.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge a gun is to load it, so doing so once more is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Stops working in Irish county seats

parts.note: Down is a county in Northern Ireland
stools are seats

explanation.surface: Workers in an Irish county take a break on their chairs.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To down tools is an idiom for going on strike or stopping work.

clue.text: Exclusive company taken in by concession

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside the following word

parts.note: a sop is a concession made to placate someone

explanation.surface: A firm accepts a concession offered to it.
explanation.definitionFit: In journalism an exclusive is a story one paper gets first, also called a scoop.

clue.text: Promote more

definitions.meaning: to promote a cause is to advance it
more in the sense of additional, extra

explanation.surface: A terse demand to advance someone again.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as a verb meaning advance or forward, and as an adjective meaning additional.

clue.text: Independent European country importing fish

indicators.note: importing means bringing in, so the fish goes inside the country

parts.note: France is a European country
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A self-governing European nation brings in fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-employed worker not tied to one employer is independent.

clue.text: Regret adopting son's cunning plan

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the son is held inside

parts.note: to rue is to regret
S is the abbreviation for son; the 's is part of the surface

explanation.surface: A parent regrets adopting a boy who turned out scheming.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse is a trick or stratagem, a synonym for a cunning plan.

clue.text: Troublemaker in gaol sadly supporting house

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting puts the piece underneath, after the house abbreviation
sadly signals the letters of in gaol are rearranged

explanation.surface: A troublemaker locked up, propping up the household from prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooligan is a rowdy, violent person, a troublemaker.

clue.text: Shakes, coming across river snakes

indicators.note: coming across means spanning, so the river letter sits inside

parts.note: rattles means shakes

explanation.surface: Someone trembles on spotting snakes by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattler is an informal name for a rattlesnake, so the plural means snakes.

clue.text: Depressed by a student grant

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so the low piece follows the other two

parts.note: L, the learner plate, stands for a student
depressed means low in spirits

explanation.surface: A student feels down about the size of a grant.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant a request is to permit or concede it, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Go too far, seeing 24 in public

indicators.note: in places the cross-referenced answer inside the word for public

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
the answer to 24 down, a word for 'go away'

explanation.surface: Someone oversteps the mark by telling people to clear off in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 refers to the solution of 24 down, a shooing-away exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshoot is to pass beyond a target, hence to go further than intended.

clue.text: Characteristic of a man to be very quiet in water

indicators.note: in places the musical marking inside the phrase for water

parts.note: Adam's ale is an old jokey name for water
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: Being silent while swimming is supposedly a manly trait.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam's ale is a humorous phrase for plain drinking water.
explanation.definitionFit: The laryngeal prominence in the throat is typically more visible in males, a distinguishing physical feature.

clue.text: Plant seeing first of many poorly

indicators.note: first of asks for the opening letter of the word many

parts.note: poorly means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: A garden plant is ailing, one of many in poor shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks botanical, but it means a factory or works.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant in the industrial sense is a factory, and a mill is one such works.

clue.text: Put one's foot down seeing expert cover Electra complex

indicators.note: cover means wrap around, so the expert word surrounds the rest

parts.note: an ace is an expert

indicators.note: complex signals the letters of Electra are tangled

explanation.surface: An expert analyst covers Freud's Electra complex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's foot down' suggests being firm, but here it is pressing the accelerator; 'complex' gives CELERAT and 'cover' wraps the expert round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting one's foot down on the pedal makes a car speed up, the idiom for going faster.

clue.text: Seat occupied by a professor of pop?

definitions.text: Seat occupied by a professor of pop?

parts.words: Seat occupied by a professor of pop?
parts.note: a professor holds a chair, and a professor of pop music would hold a chair in rock

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which seat a pop music academic would hold.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer's first word as the music genre: an academic's 'chair' is their professorship.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat that sways on curved runners, punningly the post of an academic in rock music.

clue.text: Reject drink

definitions.meaning: a refusal or rebuff, as a noun
to swallow a drink quickly, as in downing a pint

explanation.surface: Refuse a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: As one word it is a rebuff; as a phrasal verb it means to gulp a drink down.

clue.text: A graduate teacher full of inventive lies went down line

indicators.note: full of means the teaching degree contains the rest

parts.note: BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teacher's degree

indicators.note: inventive signals the letters of lies are made into something new

explanation.surface: A teacher who tells tall stories went down the line.
explanation.walkthrough: BEd (Bachelor of Education) is the teacher's degree; 'inventive' gives SEIL, which it is 'full of'. 'line' is a rope, not a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: Abseiling is descending a rock face on a rope, so this past tense means went down a line.

clue.text: Times will support seating areas for spectators and is ready to act

indicators.note: in a down clue support means lie underneath, so the times word follows

parts.note: stands are the seating areas at a sports ground
by means times, as in multiplication: three by four

explanation.surface: A newspaper funds spectator seating and is poised to step in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is BY, as in 3 by 4.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means remaining on alert, waiting to be called on.

clue.text: One takes cap off seeing nerve required in front of batsman

indicators.note: required in front of puts the courage word before the cricketer

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
an opener is a batsman who opens the innings in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket team needs a gutsy batsman at the top of the order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' meaning courage is British slang; in cricket the opener is the first batsman in.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadget for prising metal caps from drinks, described by what it does.

clue.text: Green fruit mostly going with favourite shellfish

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter

parts.note: a lime is a green citrus fruit
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: Unripe fruit served alongside a favourite seafood dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A limpet is a cone-shelled mollusc that clings to rocks, an example of shellfish.

clue.text: A long time entertaining National Trust representatives

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the long time holds the trust

parts.note: ages means a long time
NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, a British heritage charity

explanation.surface: Heritage charity staff host visitors over a long period.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that cares for historic houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Agents act on behalf of others, so they are representatives.

clue.text: Smoker invested in inhalant, expecting returns

indicators.note: returns says the hidden letters are read backwards
invested in means wrapped inside, so the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A smoker puts money into an inhaler, hoping for a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Smoker invested' as definition; 'invested in' is the hiding signal, so 'Smoker' alone defines. ANTE inside 'inhalANT Expecting', reversed by 'returns'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano smokes, so crosswords often call it a smoker.

clue.text: Almost missed call, being captain

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: skipped means missed out
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: Someone nearly misses a phone call while in charge of a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is a captain, so this verb form means acting as captain of a team or vessel.

clue.text: Heads eat out in case of parents

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters within the outside pair
case of asks for the outer letters of the word parents, its shell
out signals the letters of eat are put out of order

explanation.surface: Children eat outside in case their parents' heads turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes the shell of 'parents'; 'out' gives ATE, set 'in' that shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Pates is an old or jocular word for heads.

clue.text: Go away and film endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to film a scene is to shoot it

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave and record without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation used to scare off birds or animals, telling them to leave.

clue.text: Fall in love and despair!

definitions.meaning: to give one's affections away to someone
to become discouraged and give up hope

explanation.surface: A wry line on romance bringing both rapture and despair.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally suggests giving away one's affections and idiomatically means becoming discouraged.

clue.text: Tree snake seen regularly

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word seen

explanation.surface: A snake is spotted in a tree from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of 'seen', E and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A species of poplar with trembling leaves, an example of a tree.

clue.text: Ledger shows father with new boy fine

parts.note: da is an informal word for father

indicators.note: new signals the letters of boy are made over

parts.note: OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: An account book shows a dad with a new son doing well.
explanation.definitionFit: A diary-style account book where transactions are recorded daily, a type of ledger.

clue.text: Detectives run from ruthless criminal

indicators.note: criminal signals the letters of the word ruthless are scrambled

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Detectives flee a merciless lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R ('run') 'from' RUTHLESS and rearrange the rest, signalled by 'criminal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleuths are investigators, an informal synonym for detectives.
